title: Persistence Libraries and Repositories

content.intro: In this lesson, you will learn **Persistence Libraries and Repositories** as part of **Serialization, Networking, and Application Integration**. Integration code must validate external data, handle timeouts and failure states, keep credentials outside source control, and test boundary behavior. Use the subtopics—Repository Abstractions, Data Access and Domain Models, Testing Persistence Code—as a checklist: predict what the example will do, then verify it in a project configured for the target platform.
content.why_it_matters: Professional applications need repeatable tests, clear APIs, dependable dependencies, security checks, and observable failures. Apply this concept in small steps before integrating it into a larger project.

items.title: Repository Abstractions
items.text: Repository Abstractions is part of reproducible project configuration. Declare the dependency or plugin where it belongs, preserve a compatible version set, and use the Gradle Wrapper for repeatable builds.

items.title: Data Access and Domain Models
items.text: Data Access and Domain Models should support a clear object invariant: make valid states easy to represent, restrict mutation to the intended API, and keep initialization and dependencies explicit.

items.title: Testing Persistence Code
items.text: Testing Persistence Code helps make behavior observable and repeatable. Define the expected result, include a boundary or failure case, and preserve enough diagnostic information to locate the cause without leaking sensitive data.
